blocks.text: HANGS Construction Services LLC. Invented procedures for a software demonstration.

Capitalize an item that costs $5,000.00 or more per unit, including the costs in FA-2, and will be used for more than one year. An item below the threshold is expensed, even when many are bought on one invoice.
An asset's cost is its price and every cost to deliver it and make it ready for use: freight, setup, installation and sales tax.

A repair that keeps an asset in working order, or restores it after a breakdown, is expensed to 6300 Repairs & Maintenance. Only an improvement that extends an asset's life, adds capacity or adapts it to a new use is capitalized.

Depreciate straight-line from the month an asset is placed in service, a full month in that month and through the month it is disposed of, with no salvage value. Lives for assets placed in service from July 1, 2026: heavy equipment 84 months, survey instruments 60 months, site office units 120 months, vehicles 60 months.

When an asset is sold, scrapped or traded in, remove its cost and accumulated depreciation in the month of disposal and record the proceeds. The difference from book value is a gain or loss in 7200 Gain or Loss on Disposal.
The register's cost and accumulated depreciation must equal the general ledger, account by account, after the month's entries.
The Controller reviews the roll-forward and every proposed entry. Entries are posted only after that review, by the person who posts journal entries.

The bill is already in 6300 Repairs & Maintenance (AP-10423), which is right. Take FA-107A off the register and drop draft line 5 from JE-2610-FA1; no entry is needed.

checks.title: Test NOS-5521 against the capitalization threshold
checks.detail: FA-109, 12 items for $19,393.92, is on the register as one asset; each costs $1,616.16. NOS-5521 bought 12 items at $1,616.16 each with sales tax. FA-1 tests each unit against the $5,000.00 threshold, even when many are bought on one invoice, so none of them is a fixed asset. The bill is already in 6600 Office & Computer Equipment (AP-10417), which is right. Take FA-109 off the register and drop draft line 4; keep the items on the equipment inventory list instead. No entry is needed.

checks.title: Account for FA-105, sold October 28
checks.detail: FA-105 was sold on October 28 for $12,000.00; the ledger still carries it, and no loss was recorded. The bill of sale and the register agree: Tidewater Used Modulars bought the site office trailer, Brookstone for $12,000.00. GL 1510 still holds its $36,000.00 cost, 1590 its depreciation, and nothing was booked to 7200. Under FA-4 it is depreciated through October, so accumulated depreciation at sale is $16,500.00 ($16,200.00 to September 30 plus $300.00 for October, already in RJ-03) and book value is $19,500.00. Against the $12,000.00 price that is a $7,500.00 loss. AJ-02 removes the cost and depreciation, records the proceeds as a receivable (payment was due within 10 days of pickup, after October 31) and books the loss under FA-5.

checks.title: Recompute October depreciation by method and class
checks.detail: October depreciation on the corrected register is $4,854.54; the close's entries carry $4,532.15. Every asset recomputes straight-line from its cost and life, a full month in October for those placed in service in October and for the trailer sold in October (FA-4). The register's own October column says $5,421.08, because it still depreciates the two items struck above. The close staged RJ-03 for $3,716.67 and proposed AJ-02 for $815.48 on the excavator at its booked cost. The rest, $322.39, is October's depreciation on the full cost AJ-01 capitalizes. AJ-03 books it; if AJ-01 is not approved, this entry falls away with it.

checks.title: Roll cost and accumulated depreciation forward and tie them to the ledger
checks.detail: Cost rolls from $219,600.00 to $322,389.56: $138,789.56 of additions and $36,000.00 sold. Accumulated depreciation rolls from $101,420.00 to $89,774.54. Each account equals the ledger after the proposed entries and the corrected register, to the cent (FA-6). Net book value is $232,615.02.

checks.title: Add up the open items
checks.detail: Fixed assets roll forward to $322,389.56 of cost and $232,615.02 of book value, tied to the ledger. 3 entries proposed for $63,811.95, 5 exceptions for a person. Nothing was posted.
